title: U.S. Senate · Montana

context.text: This is an open seat. On March 4, 2026, incumbent Sen. Steve Daines (R) withdrew his candidacy and endorsed Kurt Alme, who filed to run the same day; Seth Bodnar also filed as an independent that day. According to Montana Free Press, this makes the race the first Montana U.S. Senate election without an incumbent running in 40 years. Alme, Alani Bankhead and Bodnar are viewed as the leading candidates. On July 8, 2026, 17 Democratic state legislators publicly asked Bankhead and Bodnar to decide which of them would end their campaign, warning a split vote could help Republicans; neither withdrew, and the deadline to withdraw from the ballot passed on August 10, 2026, so both remain on the ballot.

candidates.name: Kurt Alme
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary on June 2, 2026; entered the race March 4, 2026 after Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana (Oct. 2025–March 2026)

summary.text: Kurt Alme is the Republican nominee for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. He is an attorney who served as U.S. Attorney for Montana, budget director under Gov. Greg Gianforte, and director of the Montana Department of Revenue under Gov. Judy Martz, before entering the race when Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Colorado in 1989 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 1992.
Was a partner at the law firm Crowley Fleck.
Served as director of the Montana Department of Revenue under Gov. Judy Martz (R) and as budget director under Gov. Greg Gianforte (R).
Served as U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana from October 7, 2025 until leaving office on March 4, 2026 to run for Senate.

priorities.text: Says he is running to protect veterans, defend the Second Amendment, keep transgender girls and women out of women's and girls' sports, support farmers and ranchers, protect public lands, and secure elections.

candidates.name: Alani Bankhead
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026.

summary.text: Alani Bankhead is the Democratic nominee for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. She is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and counterintelligence agent who later founded a life-coaching company, running on housing, healthcare and government accountability.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and Latin American studies from Pennsylvania State University in 2004 and a graduate degree from Troy University in 2012.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2004, working as a counterintelligence agent and rising to lieutenant colonel over roughly 21 years of service.
Founded a life-coaching company called Mighty Sparrow Coaching.

priorities.text: Running on housing, healthcare, and government accountability.
"After 21 years of serving, I was looking at my beautiful state and country burning and I knew I had a special set of skills to offer the people of Montana."

candidates.name: Seth Bodnar
candidates.ballotNote: Filed as an independent on March 4, 2026, the same day Sen. Steve Daines withdrew.
candidates.currentRole: Former president of the University of Montana

summary.text: Seth Bodnar is an independent candidate for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. He is a former Green Beret, General Electric executive and University of Montana president who argues both major parties have failed the state.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the United States Military Academy at West Point and two master's degrees from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar and Truman Scholar.
Served as a Green Beret in the U.S. Army beginning in 1997.
Worked as a manager and executive at General Electric.
Served as president of the University of Montana.

priorities.text: "This country is in crisis, and our national political parties are failing us. Montanans are an independent people, and they deserve an independent voice fighting for them in Washington, DC. I'm not a politician, I'm a soldier, a businessman, a husband, a father."

candidates.name: Kyle Austin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party primary on June 2, 2026; previously a Libertarian candidate in 2022 and 2024.

summary.text: Kyle Austin is the Libertarian Party nominee for the open Montana U.S. Senate seat. He is a pharmacist and founder of the pharmacy company Pharm406.

background.text: Born in Havre, Montana, and graduated from Havre High School in 2001.
Earned a doctorate in pharmacy from the University of Montana Pharmacy School in 2008.
Worked as a pharmacist and founded his own company, Pharm406.
